exposure: Mode of birth (Cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
Infant gut microbiome vs. maternal gut microbiome
cohort: The study involved a cohort of 20 infants whose gut microbiomes were modeled at four time points during their first year of life, along with 13 maternal gut microbiome samples.
finding: The study found that infant gut microbiomes delivered via Cesarean section have perturbed metabolic functions and depleted metabolites early in life compared to vaginally delivered infants, though these differences become comparable later in the first year.
mod_finding: The gut microbiomes of infants delivered via Cesarean section demonstrated depleted metabolic capabilities and specific metabolites at the earliest stages compared to vaginal delivery, with these differences becoming comparable later in the first year.
